stem: The system of local self-government in rural India is known as the:
solution: Panchayati Raj is the system of rural local self-government in India.

stem: The Gram Sabha consists of:
options: All the voters (adult members) of the village
solution: The Gram Sabha is made up of all adult voters registered in the area of a Gram Panchayat.

stem: The elected head of a Gram Panchayat is usually called the:
solution: The head of a Gram Panchayat is the Sarpanch (also called Pradhan in some states).

stem: Members of the Gram Panchayat who are elected from different wards of the village are called:
solution: The elected ward members of a Gram Panchayat are known as Panches.

stem: The Panchayati Raj system in India has how many tiers/levels?
solution: Panchayati Raj is a three-tier system: Gram Panchayat (village), Panchayat Samiti/Block (intermediate) and Zila Parishad (district).

stem: The highest tier of the Panchayati Raj system, at the district level, is the:
solution: The Zila Parishad operates at the district level, the top tier of the three-tier Panchayati Raj structure.

stem: Which of the following is a key function of a Gram Panchayat?
options: Providing local services like water supply, streetlights and sanitation
solution: Gram Panchayats handle local civic matters such as water, cleanliness, roads, streetlights and local development.

stem: Reservation of seats for women in Panchayati Raj institutions was introduced to:
options: Ensure the participation of women in local governance
solution: Reservation of seats (at least one-third, raised to one-half in many states) ensures women's participation and representation in local self-government.

stem: The three tiers of Panchayati Raj, from village to district, are:
options: Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti (Block), Zila Parishad
Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, Vidhan Sabha
solution: The THREE TIERS of Panchayati Raj are the GRAM PANCHAYAT (village level), the PANCHAYAT SAMITI or Block (intermediate level), and the ZILA PARISHAD (district level). So option 1 is correct.

stem: The middle (intermediate) tier of Panchayati Raj, at the block level, is the:
solution: The MIDDLE (intermediate) tier of Panchayati Raj, at the BLOCK level, is the PANCHAYAT SAMITI (also called Block/Mandal Panchayat). So option 1 is correct.

stem: The lowest tier of Panchayati Raj, at the village level, is the:
solution: The LOWEST tier of Panchayati Raj, at the VILLAGE level, is the GRAM PANCHAYAT. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Gram Sabha is important because it:
options: Allows all adult villagers to directly discuss and decide local matters
solution: The GRAM SABHA is important because it allows ALL ADULT VILLAGERS to DIRECTLY DISCUSS and DECIDE local matters — a form of direct democracy at the village level. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Gram Sabha keeps a check on the Gram Panchayat by:
options: Reviewing its work, budgets and plans
solution: The GRAM SABHA keeps a CHECK on the Gram Panchayat by REVIEWING its WORK, BUDGETS, and PLANS — holding it accountable to the villagers. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment (1992) is important because it:
options: Gave constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj system
solution: The 73RD CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT (1992) gave CONSTITUTIONAL STATUS to the PANCHAYATI RAJ system, strengthening rural local self-government across India. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Members of the Gram Panchayat are chosen by:
options: Election by the villagers (the Gram Sabha)
solution: Members of the GRAM PANCHAYAT are CHOSEN by ELECTION by the VILLAGERS (the voters of the Gram Sabha), making them accountable to the people. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following is a source of income for a Gram Panchayat?
options: Local taxes, fees and government grants
solution: A GRAM PANCHAYAT gets income from LOCAL TAXES (on houses, markets, etc.), FEES, and GRANTS from the state and central government. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Reservation of seats in panchayats is provided not only for women but also for:
solution: Reservation of panchayat seats is provided for WOMEN and also for SCHEDULED CASTES (SC) and SCHEDULED TRIBES (ST), ensuring representation of disadvantaged groups. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following is a function of the Gram Panchayat?
options: Maintaining roads, drains, wells, and keeping records like births and deaths
Printing textbooks for the whole country
solution: The GRAM PANCHAYAT MAINTAINS local ROADS, DRAINS, WELLS, streetlights, and keeps RECORDS such as BIRTHS and DEATHS — attending to the village's everyday needs. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Sarpanch works together with the:
options: Ward members (Panches) and the Gram Sabha
solution: The SARPANCH works together with the WARD MEMBERS (PANCHES) and is answerable to the GRAM SABHA in running the village's affairs. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Panchayat Secretary is a person who:
options: Is a government official who keeps records and helps run the panchayat
solution: The PANCHAYAT SECRETARY is a GOVERNMENT OFFICIAL (not elected) who KEEPS RECORDS, maintains accounts, and HELPS RUN the panchayat's work. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Why is local self-government in villages important?
options: It lets villagers solve their own problems and take part in their own development
It keeps decisions far from villagers
It gives power only to the capital
solution: Local self-government in villages is important because it lets VILLAGERS SOLVE their OWN PROBLEMS and take PART in their OWN DEVELOPMENT, since they best understand local needs. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The idea behind Panchayati Raj reflects the vision of leaders like Mahatma Gandhi, who spoke of:
solution: PANCHAYATI RAJ reflects Mahatma Gandhi's vision of GRAM SWARAJ (VILLAGE SELF-RULE) — self-reliant, self-governing villages as the foundation of Indian democracy. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Zila Parishad works at the district level to:
options: Coordinate and oversee development work across the district's panchayats
solution: The ZILA PARISHAD works at the DISTRICT level to COORDINATE and OVERSEE DEVELOPMENT WORK across the district's panchayats and blocks. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Consider the pairs: 1. Gram Panchayat — village level 2. Panchayat Samiti — block level 3. Zila Parishad — district level. How many are correctly matched?
solution: ALL THREE are correct: GRAM PANCHAYAT (VILLAGE level), PANCHAYAT SAMITI (BLOCK level), and ZILA PARISHAD (DISTRICT level). So option 1 is correct.

stem: How often are elections generally held for Panchayati Raj institutions?
solution: Elections for PANCHAYATI RAJ institutions are generally held every FIVE YEARS, ensuring regular, accountable local government. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The participation of women as Sarpanches and members has helped to:
options: Bring women's concerns into local decision-making
solution: The PARTICIPATION of WOMEN as Sarpanches and members has helped BRING WOMEN's CONCERNS (like water, health, and safety) INTO LOCAL DECISION-MAKING and empowered them. So option 1 is correct.

stem: A key benefit of the Gram Sabha meeting is that villagers can:
options: Question the panchayat and take part in planning village development
solution: At a GRAM SABHA meeting, villagers can QUESTION the PANCHAYAT and TAKE PART in PLANNING village development — direct participation that keeps local government accountable. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Assertion (A): The Gram Sabha is a form of direct democracy. Reason (R): In it, all adult villagers themselves discuss and decide matters, not through representatives. Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
solution: A is TRUE — the Gram Sabha is a form of direct democracy. R is TRUE and correctly EXPLAINS A: in it, ALL ADULT VILLAGERS THEMSELVES discuss and decide matters DIRECTLY, not through representatives — which is exactly what direct democracy means. So R is the correct explanation of A. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between the Gram Sabha and the Gram Panchayat?
options: The Gram Sabha (all voters) elects and oversees the Gram Panchayat (elected body)
The Gram Panchayat elects the voters
The Gram Sabha rules the whole country
solution: The GRAM SABHA (ALL VOTERS of the village) ELECTS and OVERSEES the GRAM PANCHAYAT (the elected executive body). The Gram Panchayat is accountable to the Gram Sabha. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The word 'Panchayat' originally referred to an assembly of:
options: Five (panch) respected persons who settled village matters
solution: The word PANCHAYAT comes from 'PANCH' (five) — traditionally an ASSEMBLY of FIVE respected persons who SETTLED village disputes and matters. So option 1 is correct.

stem: A 'ward' in the context of a Gram Panchayat is:
options: A division of the village from which a Panch is elected
solution: A WARD is a DIVISION of the village from which a PANCH (ward member) is ELECTED to the Gram Panchayat. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following is an example of development work a Gram Panchayat might undertake?
options: Building village roads, wells and drains
solution: A GRAM PANCHAYAT undertakes local DEVELOPMENT WORK such as BUILDING village ROADS, WELLS, and DRAINS — improving daily life in the village. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Why must the Gram Panchayat present its budget and accounts to the Gram Sabha?
options: To ensure transparency and accountability to the villagers
solution: The Gram Panchayat presents its BUDGET and ACCOUNTS to the GRAM SABHA to ensure TRANSPARENCY and ACCOUNTABILITY to the VILLAGERS, who can then question and approve them. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Local self-government is called 'self-government' because:
options: Local people govern their own affairs through their elected representatives
solution: It is called 'SELF-GOVERNMENT' because LOCAL PEOPLE GOVERN their OWN AFFAIRS through representatives they themselves elect, rather than being ruled from outside. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The reservation of one-third (or one-half) of panchayat seats for women is significant because it:
options: Increases women's participation and leadership in rural governance
solution: Reserving one-third (or one-half in many states) of panchayat seats for WOMEN significantly INCREASES women's PARTICIPATION and LEADERSHIP in rural governance. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following matters would a Gram Panchayat typically handle?
options: Cleaning the village, maintaining ponds, and running the local primary school or anganwadi support
solution: A GRAM PANCHAYAT typically handles LOCAL matters — CLEANING the village, maintaining PONDS and wells, and supporting local schools and anganwadis — not national tasks like defence or the economy. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Gram Sabha usually meets:
options: A few times a year to discuss village issues
solution: The GRAM SABHA usually MEETS a FEW TIMES a YEAR to DISCUSS village issues, review the panchayat's work, and plan development. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following is a duty of villagers towards their panchayat?
options: Attending Gram Sabha meetings and paying local taxes
solution: Villagers' DUTIES towards their panchayat include ATTENDING GRAM SABHA meetings, PAYING local TAXES, and cooperating in village development. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The three-tier panchayat system helps because it:
options: Connects villages, blocks and districts for planning and development
solution: The THREE-TIER panchayat system CONNECTS VILLAGES, BLOCKS, and DISTRICTS, enabling coordinated PLANNING and DEVELOPMENT from the grassroots upward. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Members elected to the Zila Parishad represent:
solution: Members elected to the ZILA PARISHAD represent the WHOLE DISTRICT's RURAL AREAS, coordinating development across the district. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following is true about Panchayati Raj elections?
options: They are conducted by the State Election Commission
They are held once in fifty years
solution: PANCHAYATI RAJ elections are conducted by the STATE ELECTION COMMISSION, ensuring free and fair local elections, generally every five years. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Panchayati Raj brings democracy closer to the people because it:
options: Allows ordinary villagers to govern and develop their own villages
Gives power only to the centre
solution: PANCHAYATI RAJ brings democracy CLOSER to the PEOPLE by allowing ORDINARY VILLAGERS to GOVERN and DEVELOP their OWN VILLAGES through elected local bodies. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The role of the Sarpanch includes:
options: Presiding over panchayat meetings and leading village development
Judging court cases in the Supreme Court
solution: The SARPANCH PRESIDES over panchayat MEETINGS and LEADS VILLAGE DEVELOPMENT work, acting as the elected head of the Gram Panchayat. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following correctly pairs a body with its members?
options: Gram Sabha → all adult voters; Gram Panchayat → elected Sarpanch and Panches
Gram Sabha → only the Sarpanch; Gram Panchayat → all villagers
solution: The correct pairing is: GRAM SABHA → ALL ADULT VOTERS of the village; GRAM PANCHAYAT → the ELECTED SARPANCH and PANCHES (ward members). So option 1 is correct.

stem: Local governance improves accountability because:
options: Elected members live among the people and can be directly questioned
solution: LOCAL GOVERNANCE improves accountability because ELECTED MEMBERS LIVE AMONG the PEOPLE and can be DIRECTLY QUESTIONED about their work in the Gram Sabha. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The success of Panchayati Raj depends largely on:
options: Active participation of villagers in Gram Sabha meetings
solution: The SUCCESS of PANCHAYATI RAJ depends largely on the ACTIVE PARTICIPATION of VILLAGERS in Gram Sabha meetings, since their involvement keeps the system alive and accountable. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following best explains why local government is needed in addition to state and central government?
options: Local bodies understand and can quickly address local needs that distant governments cannot
State government can do everything alone
solution: LOCAL GOVERNMENT is needed because LOCAL BODIES UNDERSTAND and can QUICKLY ADDRESS LOCAL NEEDS (water, roads, sanitation) that DISTANT state and central governments cannot handle as effectively. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The empowerment of women through panchayats has led to:
options: More attention to issues like water, health, sanitation and children's welfare
solution: The EMPOWERMENT of WOMEN through panchayats has led to MORE ATTENTION to issues like WATER, HEALTH, SANITATION, and CHILDREN's WELFARE — reflecting women's priorities in local development. So option 1 is correct.

stem: A village that manages its own resources and solves its problems through its panchayat reflects the ideal of:
solution: A village that MANAGES its OWN resources and SOLVES its PROBLEMS through its panchayat reflects the ideal of SELF-RELIANT, SELF-GOVERNING VILLAGES — Gandhi's vision of GRAM SWARAJ. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Grassroots Democracy – Part 2: Local Government in Rural Areas' is that:
options: Rural India is governed by the PANCHAYATI RAJ system — a THREE-TIER structure of GRAM PANCHAYAT (village), PANCHAYAT SAMITI (block) and ZILA PARISHAD (district), given constitutional status by the 73rd Amendment; the GRAM SABHA (all adult villagers) is a form of direct democracy that elects and oversees the Gram Panchayat, headed by the elected SARPANCH with ward members (Panches); panchayats provide local services (water, roads, sanitation, records) funded by local taxes and grants, hold elections every five years, and RESERVE seats for women, SCs and STs — bringing self-government and participation right to the village level
solution: The chapter's overall message is that RURAL India is governed by the PANCHAYATI RAJ system — a THREE-TIER structure of the GRAM PANCHAYAT (VILLAGE level), the PANCHAYAT SAMITI (BLOCK level), and the ZILA PARISHAD (DISTRICT level) — which was given CONSTITUTIONAL STATUS by the 73RD AMENDMENT (1992). The GRAM SABHA, made up of ALL ADULT VILLAGERS, is a form of DIRECT DEMOCRACY that ELECTS and OVERSEES the GRAM PANCHAYAT, headed by the elected SARPANCH along with ward members (PANCHES) and assisted by a Panchayat Secretary. Panchayats provide LOCAL SERVICES (water, roads, sanitation, streetlights, and records like births and deaths), funded by LOCAL TAXES and government GRANTS; they hold ELECTIONS every FIVE YEARS and RESERVE seats for WOMEN, SCs, and STs — bringing self-government and PARTICIPATION right down to the village level, in the spirit of Gandhi's Gram Swaraj. So the overall message is option 2.

stem: The basic unit of rural local self-government in India is the:
solution: The Gram Panchayat is the basic (village-level) unit of Panchayati Raj, responsible for the local governance and development of one or more villages.

stem: The assembly of all adult voters of a village (or panchayat area) is called the:
solution: The Gram Sabha is the assembly of all registered voters in the area of a Gram Panchayat; it is the foundation of village democracy where villagers directly participate.

stem: The elected head of a Gram Panchayat is commonly called the:
solution: The Sarpanch (also called Pradhan or Mukhiya in some states) is the elected head of the Gram Panchayat, presiding over its meetings and coordinating village development.

stem: The members of a Gram Panchayat, elected from different wards of the village, are called:
solution: The elected members of a Gram Panchayat are called Panch or Ward Members, each representing a ward (division) of the village.

stem: The Sarpanch and Panch are elected by:
solution: The Sarpanch and Panch are directly elected by the adult voters of the village (the Gram Sabha), making the Gram Panchayat a democratically elected body.

stem: The Gram Sabha's role includes:
options: Approving the panchayat's plans, budgets and beneficiary lists, and holding it accountable
solution: The Gram Sabha discusses and approves the panchayat's development plans, budget and lists of beneficiaries for welfare schemes, and holds the Gram Panchayat accountable — participatory democracy in action.

stem: The permanent official who keeps records and assists the Gram Panchayat is the:
solution: The Panchayat Secretary is a government-appointed official who maintains records, prepares accounts and assists the Gram Panchayat in its functioning.

stem: Which of the following is a typical function of a Gram Panchayat?
options: Providing clean drinking water, sanitation, street lighting and local roads
solution: Gram Panchayats handle local civic functions — drinking water, sanitation, street lighting, village roads, drainage, and maintaining local records and welfare schemes.

stem: The main sources of income for a Gram Panchayat include local taxes and:
options: Grants from the state and central governments
solution: Gram Panchayats earn from local taxes (on houses, markets, water) and fees, and receive grants and funds from the state and central governments for development works.

stem: The second tier of Panchayati Raj, at the block/intermediate level, is the:
solution: The Panchayat Samiti (also called Block Panchayat, Mandal or Taluka Panchayat) is the intermediate tier that coordinates the Gram Panchayats within a block.

stem: The third and highest tier of Panchayati Raj, at the district level, is the:
solution: The Zila Parishad is the district-level (apex) tier of Panchayati Raj, coordinating the Panchayat Samitis and overseeing rural development across the district.

stem: Reservation of one-third (or one-half) of seats for women in the Gram Panchayat aims to:
options: Ensure women's participation and leadership in village governance
solution: Reserving seats for women ensures their active participation and leadership in local governance, giving voice to women's issues and empowering them at the grassroots.

stem: A Gram Sabha meeting must be held at least:
options: A few times a year (as prescribed, e.g. twice or more)
solution: Gram Sabha meetings are held periodically (as prescribed by state law, typically two to four times a year) so that villagers can participate in and monitor local governance.

stem: Quorum requirements for a Gram Sabha meeting ensure that:
options: A minimum number of members must be present for decisions to be valid
solution: A quorum (minimum required attendance) ensures that Gram Sabha decisions reflect the participation of a reasonable number of villagers, lending them legitimacy.

stem: One key advantage of the Gram Sabha is that it allows:
options: Every villager to directly voice concerns and participate in decisions
Decisions to be made far away
solution: The Gram Sabha empowers every adult villager to directly participate, raise issues, question the panchayat and take part in decisions — the purest form of participatory democracy.

stem: The Gram Panchayat prepares plans for the ______ of the village.
solution: Gram Panchayats prepare and implement plans for the economic development and social justice of the village, as envisaged in the 73rd Amendment and Eleventh Schedule.

stem: The MGNREGA scheme, which guarantees rural employment, is largely implemented through:
solution: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) is implemented largely through Gram Panchayats, which identify works and provide employment locally.

stem: 'Social audit' by the Gram Sabha helps to:
options: Examine and verify the panchayat's spending and works, checking corruption
solution: A social audit lets the Gram Sabha and villagers scrutinise the panchayat's records, expenditures and works (e.g. under MGNREGA), promoting transparency and checking corruption.

stem: Which section of society particularly benefits from reservation in panchayats?
options: Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and women
solution: Reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and women ensures that historically marginalised groups gain representation and a voice in village governance.

stem: The Gram Panchayat maintains records such as:
options: Birth and death registers, and records of village land and assets
solution: Gram Panchayats maintain important local records including birth and death registrations, and details of village assets, land and development works.

stem: The Panchayat Samiti coordinates the work of:
options: The Gram Panchayats within a block
solution: The Panchayat Samiti (block level) coordinates and supervises the Gram Panchayats in its block and implements development schemes at the block level.

stem: The Zila Parishad is headed by an elected chairperson often called the:
solution: The Zila Parishad is headed by an elected chairperson (President/Adhyaksha), who leads district-level rural governance and planning.

stem: Panchayats are meant to promote 'self-reliance' in villages by:
options: Planning and managing local resources and development themselves
solution: Panchayats promote village self-reliance by planning and managing local resources, works and welfare schemes according to local needs and priorities.

stem: When there is a dispute in the village, the Gram Panchayat can:
options: Help resolve minor local disputes and maintain harmony
solution: Gram Panchayats help settle minor local disputes and maintain village harmony, in addition to their development and civic functions.

stem: The success of Panchayati Raj depends greatly on:
options: Active participation of villagers in the Gram Sabha and honest local leadership
solution: Panchayati Raj works best when villagers actively participate in Gram Sabha meetings, demand accountability, and elect honest, capable local leaders.

stem: The reservation of the post of Sarpanch (chairperson) for women and SC/ST is done through:
solution: Reserved chairperson posts are rotated among different panchayats at each election, so that over time many panchayats are headed by women and SC/ST leaders.

stem: A major purpose of local self-government at the village level is to:
options: Ensure development works reach the people who need them, with their participation
solution: Village-level self-government ensures that development reaches people directly and reflects their needs, with local participation improving planning, delivery and accountability.

stem: 'Panchayat (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996' (PESA) extends Panchayati Raj to:
options: Scheduled (tribal) areas with special provisions for tribal self-governance
solution: PESA (1996) extends Panchayati Raj provisions to Scheduled Areas, empowering Gram Sabhas of tribal communities to manage their natural resources and preserve their traditions.

stem: Which statement about the Gram Panchayat is correct? (i) It is the basic unit of rural local government (ii) Its head is the Sarpanch (iii) It is elected by villagers
solution: All three are correct: the Gram Panchayat is the basic rural local government unit, headed by an elected Sarpanch, and its members are elected by the villagers.

stem: The overall aim of the Gram Sabha and Gram Panchayat system is to:
options: Deepen democracy by involving villagers in governing themselves
solution: The Gram Sabha and Gram Panchayat deepen democracy by enabling villagers to govern their own affairs, plan their development and hold their representatives accountable at the grassroots.
